tagline: A Caspian capital whose bay, islands and boulevard front an inland sea
summary: Baku wraps around a south-facing bay on the Absheron peninsula, its Seaside Boulevard already running daily excursion boats on the Caspian. The city's leisure growth, though, is on the far northern shore of the peninsula -- the master-planned Sea Breeze resort city, the White Beach and Amburan clubs, and the Bilgah beach hotels -- reachable today only by a long road loop around the headland. Rounding the Absheron tip by water collapses that trip and connects the capital directly to its new coast, with a southern link to the relocated Port of Baku at Alat.

demand_signals.label: Baku Boulevard waterfront
demand_signals.note: A flagship promenade drawing residents and visitors along the bay, with no on-water leisure product beyond occasional pleasure craft.

demand_signals.label: Boyuk Zira (Nargin) island
demand_signals.note: The bay's largest island, subject of redevelopment plans, currently without scheduled passenger access.

demand_signals.label: Absheron coast corridor
demand_signals.note: Sumqayit and the Bilgah beach districts sit along a congested peninsula road that a coastal water leg could bypass.

demand_signals.label: Trans-Caspian potential
demand_signals.note: The Aktau/Kuryk shore lies across the Caspian, a long-horizon crossing anchoring Azerbaijan's role in the Middle Corridor.

use_cases.title: Bay boulevard circuit
use_cases.body: On-demand leisure runs along the Baku Boulevard bay give the waterfront an on-water product to match its promenade showpiece.

use_cases.title: Island access shuttle
use_cases.body: A scheduled link to Boyuk Zira (Nargin) unlocks the bay's largest island for leisure and future redevelopment access.

use_cases.title: Peninsula coast bypass
use_cases.body: A coastal water leg toward Sumqayit and the Bilgah beaches offers a bypass of the congested Absheron road.

use_cases.title: Waterfront event connector
use_cases.body: Baku's marquee events along the bayfront can be served by water shuttles linking hotels, the boulevard and venues.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Suited to the sheltered 1–5 nm bay hops — boulevard circuits, Nargin island, waterfront connectors — where enclosed water and short legs favour a fast, quiet, zero-wake craft on a showpiece promenade.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Matches the longer Absheron-coast runs toward Sumqayit and Bilgah, and anchors the long-horizon trans-Caspian crossing toward Aktau/Kuryk where range is decisive.

signature_routes: Baku Boulevard bay circuit — waterfront leisure loop along the promenade
Baku ↔ Boyuk Zira (Nargin) — shuttle to the bay's largest island
Baku ↔ Sumqayit — Absheron coast bypass of the peninsula road
transit_planning: Baku's transport investment has focused on metro expansion and Absheron ring roads; the bay and peninsula coast remain without a passenger-vessel layer despite the Boulevard's status as a national waterfront showpiece. A structured marine layer adds the bay, island and coastal corridors the land network does not serve.

journeys.today: No scheduled passenger access to the island
journeys.with_navier: Scheduled shuttle across the sheltered bay, ~15 min
Coastal water bypass of the peninsula road

journeys.today: Long road detour around the peninsula

competitive_landscape: Baku's bay carries occasional pleasure craft but no organised, scheduled passenger-vessel operator; the island and peninsula-coast corridors are entirely unserved by water. Land-side ride-hail is mature, and the Boulevard is a flagship promenade — yet the on-water layer is absent, an unusually clean structural gap on a national showpiece waterfront.
seasonality: The Caspian's strong northerly Khazri wind can raise short, steep chop across the bay in winter and shoulder months; the enclosed inner bay along the Boulevard stays workable most of the year, while exposed Absheron-coast and any trans-Caspian legs are seasonally wind-gated. Summer is peak for waterfront leisure.
regulatory_note: Caspian passenger navigation falls under Azerbaijan's maritime administration; the Caspian's special legal status among littoral states shapes any cross-sea (trans-Caspian) operation, keeping such crossings a coordinated long-horizon prospect. Bay and coastal operations sit within domestic licensing, and waterfront access aligns with the Boulevard authority.

precedents.why_it_matters: A national showpiece bayfront with heavy footfall but no on-water product — a ready leisure market for scheduled water mobility.
Planned island redevelopment implies future access demand a scheduled shuttle can anchor.
